requirement:
Colon-fenced directive bodies are outlined recursively as Markdown. Ordinary
fenced code-block contents remain literal, creating no nested paragraph or
directive nodes. Backtick fences with a directive name such as `{note}` in
their info string are literal code blocks.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover all three obligations in `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fenced_blocks.contents`. All of them are in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/markdown_tests.rs` and carry a {test} reference to the subject. I did not read the implementation.

**1. Colon-fenced directive bodies are outlined recursively as Markdown.**
- `paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges` has a `::::{note}` block that holds a paragraph and a nested `:::{tip}` block. The tip block holds its own paragraph. The test asserts the exact node kinds, parents and line ranges. It also checks that selectors resolve and that node text matches the source slice.
- `unfinished_directives_retain_their_body_and_leave_the_outer_closer_outside` covers unterminated directives and a nested directive inside a longer outer fence. It asserts that paragraphs exist and that the inner and outer blocks have the right parents and ranges.
- `empty_long_closed_and_quoted_directives_keep_original_unicode_offsets` covers a directive inside a blockquote, with CRLF line endings and Unicode text. It asserts a paragraph inside the nested directive.

**2. Ordinary fenced code-block contents stay literal, with no nested paragraph or directive nodes.**
- `literal_code_inline_code_and_html_shield_directive_looking_text` uses a ```` fence and a `~~~~` fence. Each contains `:::{note}` plus a shorter fence line. The test asserts exactly one block and no paragraph.
- `unfinished_code_fences_remain_literal_blocks_through_eof` covers unclosed backtick and tilde fences containing `:::{note}`. It asserts one block, no children, no paragraph, and a range that runs to EOF.
- `nested_fence_lengths_and_closer_whitespace_preserve_the_right_containers` has a `~~~text` fence inside an outer directive. The fence contains `::::::` and `:::{fake}`. The test asserts only three blocks, so the `:::{fake}` text creates no block, and that `owner_at_line(12)` is a block.
- `paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges` includes a plain ```` ```text ```` block, which appears as a leaf block with no paragraph child.

**3. Backtick fences with a directive name such as `{note}` in the info string are literal code blocks.**
- `literal_code_inline_code_and_html_shield_directive_looking_text` includes the source `` ```{note}\n:::{tip}\nBody.\n:::\n``` ``. It asserts exactly one block and no paragraph, so neither the info string nor the inner `:::{tip}` creates a directive or nested content.

A wrong implementation would fail at least one of these tests. If it treated a code fence's contents as Markdown, it would produce paragraphs or nested blocks. If it treated a `{note}` backtick fence as a directive, or skipped recursion into a directive, the node-kind and parent assertions would fail. I found no untested obligation in the requirement text.
